newsitem.title: NORWAY: Nycomed in Oslo dismisses market rumours.
newsitem.headline: Nycomed in Oslo dismisses market rumours.

text.p: Norwegian pharmaceuticals group Nycomed ASA on Thursday dismissed rumours which had sent its share price falling more than seven percent.
Alex Gundersen, Vice President for investor relations, said rumours circulating in the Norwegian and international markets were without basis.
Nycomed's A and B stock fell 5.50 crowns in moderate turnover to close at 72 crowns and 70 crowns respectively.
Brokers attributed the downward slide to rumours of a large seller in the stock and to intensified price pressure in the U.S. market for Nycomed's major X-ray diagnostic imaging products.
"There have been several rumours in the market today and I find it necessary to state that all of them are totally without any basis," Gundersen told Reuters.
Nycomed announced in August a six percent dip in first-half operating revenues due to strong price pressure in the U.S. market for diagnostic cantrast agents and in its therapeutic business.

"The market already knows about the tough price competition in the U.S. There has been no new information on the U.S. pricing situation that can explain today's movement and there is also no new information fundamentally to explain the move," Gundersen said.

"My own speculation is that the market has entered a wait and see mode on Nycomed and that has resulted in low liquidity. Obviously there were a couple of sellers this morning and that together with the low liquidity acted to exaggerate the price movement," he said.
